name: Bronte: the park behind the beach, its promenade, the Bogey Hole and the baths, and the flats round 499 Bronte Rd

plants.why: Canary Island date palms along the park's side of the Beach Promenade, as the listing's aerial photos of 499 Bronte Rd show them (02, 06, 13)
Norfolk Island pines along the park's south edge above Calga Place, and at the corner by the steps up to Bronte Rd (02, 13)
Norfolk Island pines in the park's lawn, the tallest trees there in the photos

rock.why: The rock shelf at the beach's south end round the Bogey Hole, the pool among the rocks (OSM's swimming area, way 592332752), which OSM doesn't draw as rock
The shelf past Bronte Baths, under the cliff

buildings.why: The blocks of flats along Pacific St and up Bronte Rd from the beach, round 499 Bronte Rd: red brick under terracotta tiled roofs, two and three storeys (the listing's aerial photos 02 and 13). The build gave them the walk-ups' flat roofs and its houses' mix of styles.
